## Introduction

In this report we explore a dataset of movies taken from the Internet Movie Database (IMDb). The analysis has three parts: 1. We first load and describe the data 2. We preprocess the data 3. We visualise it.

## The Data

We use the `dplyr` package to manipulate the data and the `ggplot2` package to create plots.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

The data is stored in the file `CleanMovies.csv`, which we load into R.

```{r}
movies <- read.csv("CleanMovies.csv")
head(movies)
```

The dataset contains `r nrow(movies)` films and `r ncol(movies)` variables.

```{r}
nrow(movies) 
ncol(movies)

```

## Pre - processing
Before analysing the data we need to clean it. Some movies in the dataset
have a rating of 0, which suggests that they were never rated, and some
have a budget or revenue of less than one million dollars, which are
unlikely to be reliable. These would distort our results, so we remove
them using `filter()`. We also use `mutate()` to create two new
variables: the `profit` of each movie (its revenue minus its budget), and
the `decade` in which it was released.

```{r}
movies_clean <- movies |>
  filter(rating > 0 , budget >= 1, revenue >= 1) |>
  mutate(
    profit = revenue - budget,
    decade = floor(release_year / 10) * 10
  )
```

This removed 805 movies, leaving us
with 8918 movies to analyse. As a check that our new
variables make sense, here are the five most profitable movies in the
dataset:
```{r}
movies_clean |>
  slice_max(profit, n= 5) |>
  select(title, release_year, budget, revenue, profit) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
